title: Mon corps spécial
oneGoal: Students will identify basic body parts and understand that every body is unique and special
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with body vocabulary?
What visual supports are needed?
How to include diverse body representations?
progression: Foundation lesson introducing body awareness in a positive, inclusive way
realWorldConnection: Understanding our body helps us take care of ourselves and communicate our needs

title: Mes parties du corps
oneGoal: Students will name and point to major body parts using French vocabulary
decisionPoints: Are students ready for more body vocabulary?
What movement activities work best?
How to address student questions naturally?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by expanding body vocabulary with movement and songs
realWorldConnection: Knowing body parts helps us tell adults when we hurt or need help

title: Mon corps fait des choses
oneGoal: Students will understand that different body parts have different functions
decisionPoints: How are students connecting vocabulary to functions?
What sensory activities are most engaging?
Are all students participating comfortably?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by connecting body parts to their important functions
realWorldConnection: Understanding what our body parts do helps us protect them and use them safely

title: Qui peut toucher?
oneGoal: Students will understand the concept of personal space and appropriate touch
decisionPoints: How to introduce boundaries age-appropriately?
What examples resonate with students?
How to address different family cultures?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by introducing the concept that our bodies belong to us
realWorldConnection: Learning about personal space helps us feel safe and respect others

title: Touches qui aident
oneGoal: Students will distinguish between helpful touches and touches that make them uncomfortable
decisionPoints: How are students processing touch concepts?
What scenarios are most relatable?
How to handle student disclosures appropriately?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by exploring when and why people might need to touch us for help
realWorldConnection: Understanding helpful touch prepares us for medical visits and getting help when injured

title: Dire non
oneGoal: Students will practice saying 'no' clearly and understand they have the right to refuse uncomfortable touch
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with assertiveness?
What practice scenarios are appropriate?
How to balance respect with boundaries?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by empowering students to communicate their boundaries
realWorldConnection: Learning to say 'no' helps us stay safe and communicate our feelings

title: Adultes de confiance
oneGoal: Students will identify trusted adults in their lives who can help them
decisionPoints: Who are the trusted adults in each student's life?
How to include diverse family structures?
What if a student has limited trusted adults?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by identifying people who can help when we need to use our 'no'
realWorldConnection: Knowing trusted adults gives us people to talk to when we need help or feel worried

title: Chercher de l'aide
oneGoal: Students will understand when and how to seek help from trusted adults
decisionPoints: How well do students understand help-seeking?
What communication methods work best?
How to address barriers to asking for help?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by practicing how to actually ask trusted adults for help
realWorldConnection: Knowing how to ask for help keeps us safe and helps us solve problems

title: Sécurité à la maison
oneGoal: Students will identify home safety rules and safe places in their homes
decisionPoints: What are common home safety concerns for this age?
How to address different home environments?
What safety rules are most important?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by applying safety concepts to the home environment
realWorldConnection: Home safety rules protect us and our families every day

title: Sécurité à l'école
oneGoal: Students will understand school safety rules and procedures
decisionPoints: Which school safety procedures need emphasis?
How are students feeling about school safety?
What school-specific concerns exist?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by extending safety awareness to the school environment
realWorldConnection: School safety rules help everyone learn and play together safely

title: Sécurité dans la communauté
oneGoal: Students will identify community helpers and basic community safety
decisionPoints: Which community helpers are most familiar to students?
How to address community safety without fear?
What community resources exist locally?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by expanding safety awareness to the broader community
realWorldConnection: Community helpers and safety rules keep our neighborhoods safe for everyone

title: Numéros d'urgence
oneGoal: Students will learn about emergency numbers and when to use them
decisionPoints: Are students ready to learn about emergencies?
How to teach emergency response without fear?
What emergency scenarios are age-appropriate?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by introducing emergency response procedures
realWorldConnection: Knowing emergency numbers can help save lives and get help when needed

title: Sentiments et sécurité
oneGoal: Students will connect their feelings to safety and learn to trust their instincts
decisionPoints: How are students connecting feelings to safety?
What emotional vocabulary do they need?
How to validate all feelings appropriately?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by integrating emotional awareness with safety concepts
realWorldConnection: Our feelings help us know when we're safe and when we might need help

title: Portfolio de sécurité
oneGoal: Students will create their personal safety portfolio showing what they've learned
decisionPoints: How can students best demonstrate their learning?
What format works for different learners?
How to celebrate growth and learning?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing all safety learning into a personal collection
realWorldConnection: Creating a safety portfolio helps us remember important safety information

title: Jeux de rôle sécurité
oneGoal: Students will practice safety scenarios through role-play
decisionPoints: Which scenarios need more practice?
How comfortable are students with role-play?
What situations are most relevant?
progression: Extension: Provides additional practice of core safety concepts through drama
realWorldConnection: Practicing safety scenarios helps us be ready for real situations

title: Histoires de sécurité
oneGoal: Students will explore safety concepts through storytelling
decisionPoints: Which stories resonate most with students?
How to choose diverse, inclusive stories?
What discussion questions are most valuable?
progression: Extension: Reinforces safety learning through narrative and discussion
realWorldConnection: Stories help us understand how safety concepts apply in different situations

title: Art corporel positif
oneGoal: Students will create art celebrating body diversity and self-acceptance
decisionPoints: How to celebrate all body types and abilities?
What art materials work best?
How to address body image positively?
progression: Extension: Reinforces body positivity through creative expression
realWorldConnection: Art helps us express our feelings about ourselves and celebrate differences

title: Chansons de sécurité
oneGoal: Students will learn and create songs about safety concepts
decisionPoints: Which safety concepts work well in song?
What musical styles engage students?
How to make songs memorable and fun?
progression: Extension: Reinforces safety vocabulary through music and rhythm
realWorldConnection: Songs help us remember important safety rules and make learning fun

title: Famille et sécurité
oneGoal: Students will explore how different families talk about and practice safety
decisionPoints: How to honor diverse family approaches to safety?
What family sharing is appropriate?
How to support all family structures?
progression: Extension: Connects school safety learning with home and family practices
realWorldConnection: Families are important partners in keeping us safe and healthy

title: Célébration de sécurité
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their safety learning and commit to ongoing safety practices
decisionPoints: How can we celebrate learning appropriately?
What commitments are realistic for students?
How to end the unit positively and confidently?
progression: Extension: Culminates the unit with celebration and commitment to safety practices
realWorldConnection: Celebrating our learning helps us remember how important safety is in our daily lives
